sense: demand as one’s own or one’s due

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; often with sibi
evidence: Plin. Ep. 6.32.2: partem oneris tuī mihi vindicō
Traupman 291: vindicāre, claim as one’s own
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to lay claim to as one’s own”; sibi vindicāre, to claim for oneself (a share, credit, a right).

terms.gloss: claim back, ask for the return of
claim (for oneself) what is not one’s due
evidence: Cic. Brut. 292 (Lewis & Short): sapientiam sibi adrogāre

phrases.latin: Homērum Colophōniī cīvem esse dīcunt suum, Chiī suum vindicant, Salamīniī repetunt, Smyrnaeī vērō suum esse cōnfirmant
phrases.english: The people of Colophon say that Homer was their citizen, the Chians claim him as theirs, the Salaminians claim him back, and the people of Smyrna insist that he is theirs

phrases.latin: Vērum enim, quandō bene prōmeruit, fīat: suum jūs postulat.
phrases.english: Well, since he’s earned it, so be it: he’s claiming what is his by right.

sources: Lewis & Short: vindico · Lewis & Short: postulo · Lewis & Short: repeto · Lewis & Short: arrogo
Cic. Arch. 19, Plin. Ep. 6.32.2, Ter. Ad. 201 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 291.
